statement: Build a rectangular grid of points on a surface by number of cells or by cell size, as the base for any 2D paneling pattern.
superiority: Dino 8 should build grids that honour trimmed boundaries and report cell distortion, with no failures on open or periodic surfaces.

acceptance.corpus: Planar 20 x 10 m surface, 20 x 10 cells, and a trimmed freeform patch
acceptance.tolerance: Cell count exact; grid points lie on the surface within 1e-6

statement: Edit an existing grid: recentre, shift, reverse, extract rows and columns, and combine grids so patterns can be adjusted without rebuilding.
superiority: Dino 8 should treat grids as one editable type with stable indexing so downstream panels keep their identity when the grid changes.

acceptance.corpus: Grid of 30 x 30 shifted by 1 row then reversed twice
acceptance.tolerance: Index map of every point equals the expected permutation exactly

notes: Center Grid is named in the McNeel release thread; other grid-utility names were not individually found in reachable pages.

statement: Populate a grid with a 2D pattern chosen from built-in rectangular or triangular patterns so each cell gets a panel curve or surface.

source.ref: 2D paneling patterns on a rectangular grid

superiority: Dino 8 should include a visual pattern library with live preview and the same results on every platform.

acceptance.corpus: Built-in patterns on a 12 x 12 grid
acceptance.tolerance: Panel count equals analytic count per pattern; panels tile the grid with total area error < 1e-9

statement: Create brick-like and other offset patterns on a grid by building the pattern from user-defined cells, since the stock Rhino 2D options are not predefined in Grasshopper.
superiority: Dino 8 should offer ready brick, running-bond and herringbone pattern components so users need not follow manual-page recipes.

acceptance.corpus: Running-bond brick pattern 10 x 10 on a flat wall with half-brick offset
acceptance.tolerance: Row offset equals half cell width within 1e-9; no overlaps or gaps (area union equals wall area within 1e-9)

statement: Fill the space between two bounding grids with 3D modules to make thick, volumetric paneling.

source.ref: Panel3D components (3D patterns between two grids)

superiority: Dino 8 should keep module corners welded to both grids and report self-intersection so cells are fabrication-ready.

acceptance.corpus: Two parallel grids 5 m apart populated with box modules
acceptance.tolerance: Module volume sum equals prism volume within 1e-9; adjacent modules share faces exactly

statement: Morph a base module onto each grid cell so one parametric module adapts to the local cell shape across a doubly curved surface.
superiority: Dino 8 should morph with guaranteed edge continuity between neighbours and a distortion metric per module.

acceptance.corpus: Square module morphed onto 400 cells of a doubly curved surface
acceptance.tolerance: Module corners coincide with cell corners within 1e-6; neighbours share boundary curves within 1e-6

statement: Drive pattern parameters (opening size, depth, rotation) with attractors so panels vary smoothly across a facade.

source.ref: Attractors with grids and morphing patterns

superiority: Dino 8 should bind attractor falloff to panel parameters with live preview and keep the pattern deterministic.

acceptance.corpus: 100 x 40 grid, one curve attractor, linear falloff 0 to 1
acceptance.tolerance: Parameter at each cell equals analytic falloff within 1e-9

statement: Create hexagonal and other custom connection patterns from a rectangular grid by defining which grid points connect to each other.

source.ref: Custom connection from a rectangular grid (hexagonal tessellation)

superiority: Dino 8 should include hexagonal, triangular and Voronoi-like connection presets with automatic edge-case handling at grid borders.

acceptance.corpus: Hex pattern on a 20 x 20 grid
acceptance.tolerance: Interior cells are regular hexagons with side length equal within 1e-9; border cells closed cleanly

statement: Generate organic, cellular and slightly randomized panel layouts from a grid with seeded irregularity.
superiority: Dino 8 should make randomness reproducible by seed and keep cells valid and non-overlapping.

acceptance.corpus: Randomized cell layout with seed 42, 500 cells
acceptance.tolerance: Identical output on 3 runs; no overlap (pairwise intersection area < 1e-9)

notes: Related forum topics listed on the brick pattern thread describe organic, cellular configurations; exact PT-GH components were not named.

statement: Divide a surface into rectangles of several different widths in a controlled sequence for facade rationalization.
superiority: Dino 8 should accept a list of widths and a repeat rule and give a rationalization report listing unique panel sizes.

acceptance.corpus: Surface 30 m wide divided with widths 1.2, 1.5, 1.8 m repeating
acceptance.tolerance: Widths exact; remainder reported; unique size count equals 3

statement: Post-process panels for fabrication: unroll panels flat, offset them, create pipe or fin elements, and rationalize complex geometry for analysis.

source.ref: Paneling utility components (Unroll, Offset, Pipe, Fin)

superiority: Dino 8 should provide nested-layout and labeling of unrolled panels with distortion warnings, making the output cut-ready.

acceptance.tolerance: Flat edge lengths equal 3D lengths within 1e-6; area preserved within 1e-6

notes: Component group names come from the McNeel resources and release pages; the primer PDF was unreachable.

statement: Share and install paneling definitions through the package manager so documents containing paneling components open on another machine.
superiority: Dino 8 should bundle paneling natively so no package install is needed and files always open.

acceptance.corpus: Open a definition with all paneling components on a clean install
acceptance.tolerance: 0 missing components; document loads without prompts
